analyzed_vuln.description: The 1-MV motion-compensation path decides whether to use edge emulation only from the luma coordinates and luma interpolation footprint (lines 291-294), then performs an 8x8 VC-1 chroma interpolation without independently validating the 9x9 chroma source footprint. Near a chroma plane boundary this leaves srcU/srcV pointing directly into the minimally allocated reference frame. put_no_rnd_vc1_chroma_mc8_c then unconditionally evaluates src[a+1], src[stride+a], and src[stride+a+1] for every output pixel, including dst[7], causing the observed one-byte heap over-read. The DSP routine is the crashing consumer; the missing chroma bounds/edge-emulation decision in ff_vc1_mc_1mv is the root cause. The analogous 4-MV chroma path explicitly checks uvsrc_x/uvsrc_y against a 9-pixel footprint, highlighting the omitted validation.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A crafted VC-1 stream must decode a P-picture 1-MV inter macroblock (the PoV reaches this through the skipped-MB path), select the no-rounding chroma MC path (v->rnd is true), and produce a reference position whose luma footprint passes the ff_vc1_mc_1mv edge test while the corresponding 8x8 chroma block lies at a plane edge and lacks the extra neighbor column and/or row required by the unconditional bilinear loads. With the fuzzer's tightly sized per-plane reference-frame allocations, the direct srcU/srcV pointer then reaches the allocation boundary and dst[7]'s interpolation reads past it.
